summary: A ten-step guide to designing sets on a tight budget, aimed at community theaters and built around quotes from designers and directors at various theaters. Advice ranges from meticulous planning, repurposing, and partnering with local businesses and schools to multi-functional pieces, inexpensive technology, paint and lighting, creative construction, resourceful teams, community involvement, and embracing imperfection. The overall message is that limited budgets can spur creativity.
one_line: Ten practical steps, illustrated with quotes from theater professionals, for community theaters to create inventive, affordable set designs.
key_facts: Jonathan Perry has managed the Springfield Playhouse as theater director since September 12, 2023.
In a September 25 interview, Jonathan Perry said, "Tight budgets push our creativity. We find that limitation can actually be the mother of invention."
Emma Thompson, a local set designer at Greenville Community Theater, advises creating a comprehensive list of scenes and sketching designs well before rehearsals begin.
On October 5, 2023, the Riverside Theater held a 'Set Swap' meet where local theaters exchanged set pieces and props, a practice that has since grown in popularity.

Jessica Brooks of the Baytown Little Theater says local hardware stores might donate or discount materials; her theater once borrowed a full set of period furniture from a local high school after its production of 'The Crucible'.

Michael Henderson, Youngstown Playhouse's set designer, uses reversible flats and modular units that can change from a house facade to a palace wall; the theater reopened after renovation in December 2023.
Sarah Kim of the Dover Theater Collective suggests projectors for backdrops; the theater has used inexpensive LED lighting and secondhand projectors as of its last production in January 2024.
Bill Thomson, a painter and set designer, says a well-painted backdrop adds depth and texture, and cites silhouetted scenes in a late January production that relied solely on strategic lighting.
On February 18, 2024, Sandy Martinez led a workshop on creative construction, using materials like fabric and foam to create illusions.
Steve Johnson, director at the Madison Avenue Theater, says every member of his set design team is versed in DIY techniques, which saved costs on their March 2024 production.
Amanda Lee, production manager at Lakeside Theatre since April 5, 2024, said people have donated items left over from garage sales.
Actor Gordon Smith says the charm of community theater lies in its authenticity, and that the performance, not just the set, captivates audiences.
